generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: copy from the parent key pool actually written (parents generated first); for nullable FK columns plant NULL on a share matching the compact DB (at least one NULL per nullable FK); ensure some parent rows have no children
generic_sampling_rules.composite_fk: sample the child FK as a tuple from the parent's composite key set actually written (never column-by-column)
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: random word from a 200-word pool, 1-20 chars
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: random capitalized word, unique per table where UNIQUE and never overwritten by duplicates/ties
generic_sampling_rules.near_variant: for each listed literal, generate exact, lower-case, upper-case, one-char-edit, and one-char-append variants
generic_sampling_rules.boundary: for each listed numeric literal L with step s, generate L-s, L, L+s; for dates generate L-1day, L, L+1day in the column's format
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: for nullable columns, plant at least one NULL and a NULL share matching the compact database's share (5-30% unless statistics show otherwise); never replace a planted NULL to satisfy a rule; run NULL planting after dedupe and never drop NULL rows
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates: for DISTINCT-target columns, 20-50% of rows share values with another row; only for non-UNIQUE, non-PK columns
generic_sampling_rules.ties: for ORDER-target columns, ensure at least two rows share the value at the listed rank; only on columns where uniqueness is not required
generic_sampling_rules.unmatched_join: for join-target columns, ensure some parent rows have no child rows and (where nullable) some child rows carry NULL FK

issues.evidence: The NULL interface rule requires that every nullable column (including nullable FKs) contains at least one NULL row and a NULL share following the compact database's share. In `build_random_instance`, `_apply_null` (the only NULL-planting helper) is never called, and `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` only produces NULLs when the parent pool is empty. `NULL_TARGETS` is imported but unused. So nullable columns will not reliably receive NULLs, and nullable FKs will not get the required NULL share.

issues.title: Generated instances violate foreign keys (70,358 FK violations across 20/20 instances)
issues.evidence: Execution feedback: integrity.fk_violations = 70358; every instance invalid with new_fk_violations (e.g. chk_0000: 4099, chk_0017: 6769). Top offenders: Store.BusinessEntityID -> BusinessEntity.BusinessEntityID (10883 rows), SalesOrderDetail.(SpecialOfferID,ProductID) -> SpecialOfferProduct (10185), Password.BusinessEntityID -> Person.BusinessEntityID (4834), SalesPerson.BusinessEntityID -> Employee.BusinessEntityID (4670), SalesOrderHeader.ShipMethodID -> Address.AddressID (2889).
issues.requested_revision: Fix FK generation so every generated child FK value exists in the parent key pool actually written to the instance. Root causes visible in code: (1) writer.py sets `pragma foreign_keys = OFF` and silently skips rows that fail, so FK-invalid rows are committed; (2) instance.py `_parent_pools` mixes compact parent keys with generated keys, but generated parent rows are themselves frequently skipped by the writer (e.g. Person skipped 237, Employee skipped 247, BusinessEntity skipped 204, Address skipped 218), leaving child FKs pointing at never-written parents; (3) composite FK (SalesOrderDetail.SpecialOfferID,ProductID -> SpecialOfferProduct) is sampled column-by-column independently, so the pair is not guaranteed to exist. Generate FK values only from parent keys that will actually be written (or write parents first and verify), sample composite FKs as tuples from the parent's composite key set, and enable `pragma foreign_keys = ON` (or post-validate) so violations are caught rather than silently committed.

issues.title: Writer silently drops large fractions of generated rows, breaking dependencies and the NULL rule
issues.evidence: rows_skipped is large for many tables: EmailAddress 1492, EmployeePayHistory 2239, ProductCostHistory 2286, ProductInventory 2734, ProductProductPhoto 3609, ProductVendor 4047, SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason 12239, SalesOrderHeader 213, SalesOrderDetail 202, etc. Because parents are dropped after children were sampled against them, FK integrity collapses. Also, the NULL rule is not met: every nullable column reports 'NULL 0 / n' (e.g. Person.MiddleName NULL 0/1412, SalesOrderHeader.ShipDate NULL 0/5088, ProductVendor.LastReceiptCost NULL 0/14262), i.e. no planted NULLs survive.
issues.requested_revision: Stop relying on row-by-row skip as the failure mode. Diagnose why rows fail (likely UNIQUE collisions from `_apply_duplicates`/`_apply_ties`/`_apply_group_sizes` overwriting UNIQUE columns, and NOT NULL repairs in writer._fallback overwriting planted NULLs). Ensure planted NULLs on nullable columns are preserved (the writer's `_fallback` currently replaces NULLs on NOT NULL columns only, but the NULL rule requires nullable columns to keep NULLs — verify `_apply_null` runs after dedupe and that dedupe does not drop NULL rows). Reduce skip counts to near zero and re-run; the NULL-share requirement (at least one NULL per nullable column, share matching compact DB) must be observable in the written instances.

issues.title: Dangling FK warnings indicate schema reading drops real FKs
issues.evidence: stderr: 'dropping dangling FK Document.Owner -> Employee.Owner', 'SalesOrderHeader.ShipMethodID -> Address.ShipMethodID', 'SalesOrderHeader.ShipToAddressID -> Address.ShipToAddressID', 'SalesOrderHeader.BillToAddressID -> Address.BillToAddressID', 'SalesOrderHeader.SalesPersonID -> SalesPerson.SalesPersonID'. The schema in the prompt declares these as FKs to Employee.BusinessEntityID, Address.AddressID, SalesPerson.BusinessEntityID respectively. schema.py resolves the parent column via `r[4] if r[4] is not None else r[3]`, which mis-resolves when the referenced column name differs from the child column name.
issues.requested_revision: Fix FK parent-column resolution in schema.py so the referenced column is taken from the FK definition (pragma foreign_key_list column 4 is the parent column; when NULL it defaults to the parent PK, not the child column name). After the fix, SalesOrderHeader.ShipMethodID must reference ShipMethod.ShipMethodID (per the prompt schema) and the other dangling FKs must resolve; re-verify no FKs are dropped.
